title: Microsoft Teams: organisers can delete meeting recording, transcript and AI notes from the recap
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap supports organiser deletion and availability, and Microsoft documents the licensing background and the listed controls. Narrow the statement about missing Learn documentation, complete the recording-expiry path, and flag conflicting documentation about AI-summary expiry.

claims.claim: Teams has a new delete button on the meeting recap page.
claims.quote: through the new delete button in recap page.

claims.claim: Purview retention can cover files in OneDrive, SharePoint and SharePoint Embedded.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Why it matters; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: No tenant or meeting-policy switch specifically governing the recap delete button is documented on either the UI or automation surface.
claims.quote: Searched: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy prevent delete recap content meeting organizer delete recap switch. Opened the full cmdlet reference and searched delete/Recap; read memory, transcription, expiry and unsaved-transcript recap pages. No button-specific switch.

claims.claim: Non-channel meeting recordings normally save to the organiser's OneDrive.
claims.quote: For meetings and events, the recording saves to the organizer's OneDrive, even if the organizer didn't attend the meeting or event.

claims.claim: Channel meeting recordings save to the channel's SharePoint site.
claims.quote: For Channel meetings, the recording is stored in the SharePoint Teams site documentation library in a folder named Recordings.

claims.claim: When an organiser has no OneDrive, the recording falls back to a co-organiser's OneDrive or the recording initiator's OneDrive.
claims.quote: The recording is saved to the co-organizer's OneDrive ... If none of the co-organizers have OneDrive accounts, the recording is saved to the OneDrive account of the user who initiated the recording.

claims.claim: Other internal attendees normally have read access to recordings of ordinary non-channel meetings.
claims.quote: All other members of the meeting from the same organization as the organizer have read access

claims.claim: Some participants in large meetings may not receive recording access automatically.
claims.quote: For large meetings with more than 2,000 participants, some participants may not automatically receive permissions to the recording file.

claims.claim: Channel meeting recording permissions are inherited from the channel.
claims.quote: For Channel meetings, permissions are inherited from the owners and members list in the channel.

claims.claim: The button's role scope beyond the roadmap's word organisers is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams delete meeting recap content button licensing pricing meter co-organizer. Read memory and unsaved-transcript recap deletion sections; both name organisers, neither specifies additional roles for this roadmap button.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes deletion rather than new data access.
claims.quote: Meeting organizers can now easily delete meeting generated content including recording, transcript, AI summary, and notes through the new delete button in recap page. Shared files in the meeting won't be deleted.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes an organiser using a button, not automatic or agent-driven deletion.
claims.quote: Meeting organizers can now easily delete meeting generated content ... through the new delete button in recap page.

claims.claim: Users can modify the expiration date of recordings they control.
claims.quote: End users can modify the expiration date of any recordings they control, so you shouldn't rely on meeting expiration settings for legal protection.

claims.claim: Deleting or expiring a transcript or recording does not automatically delete meeting memory.
claims.quote: Meeting memory won't automatically be deleted if the transcript or recording is deleted or expired.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Intelligent recap requires Teams Premium or Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: You must assign a Teams Premium license or Microsoft Copilot license to your users.

claims.claim: AI-generated recap experiences including audio and video recap require Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: AI-generated recap experiences, including audio recap and video recap, require a Microsoft Copilot license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Generating recap without saving transcripts requires an organiser with Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: Organizers with a Microsoft Copilot license can generate AI summaries of Teams meetings without saving a recording or persistent transcript.

claims.claim: The full intelligent recap experience requires transcription.
claims.quote: To allow your users to use intelligent recap, you must turn on transcription:

claims.claim: Recap without saving transcripts can generate an AI summary when recording and transcription are not enabled.
claims.quote: With this feature, an AI summary is generated even when recording and transcription aren't enabled.

claims.claim: With recording turned off, recap lacks the recording, speakers, topics and chapters.
claims.quote: If recording is turned off, users experience recap without the recording, speakers, topics, and chapters.

claims.claim: AI summaries for recap without saved transcripts are stored in the organiser's OneDrive.
claims.quote: The AI summary is stored as a read-only Word document in the organizer's OneDrive.

claims.claim: The Transcription control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Transcription.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Meeting policies. ... Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one. ... Toggle Transcription On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscription $true enables transcription in that meeting policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowTranscription $true

claims.where: controls[1].governs and note; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Meeting-policy transcription governs whether meetings can have saved transcripts, not the recap delete button.
claims.quote: For meetings and events to include transcripts, the organizer must have this setting turned on. The user who starts the recording or transcript must also have this setting turned on.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls: recording expiry row
claims.claim: Recording expiry is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > Recording & transcription > Recordings and transcriptions automatically expire.
claims.quote: under Meetings > Meeting policies > Recording & transcription. ... After turning on Recordings and transcriptions automatically expire, you'll get the option to set the Default expiration time, measured in days.
claims.fix: Set controls[2].ui.path and its rendered path to 'Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Recording & transcription > Recordings and transcriptions automatically expire > Default expiration time'. The policy selection is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/meeting-transcription-captions; the two expiry settings are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-teams-recording-expiration-policy.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls: recording expiry row
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -NewMeetingRecordingExpirationDays <days> sets recording and transcript expiration.
claims.quote: To set the expiration time using PowerShell, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -NewMeetingRecordingExpirationDays <days>

claims.claim: Changes to recording and transcript expiration settings affect only newly created recordings and transcripts.
claims.quote: Any changes to this setting only affect newly created recordings and transcripts. You can't change the expiration time on existing meeting recordings and transcripts.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Governance controls: AI summary expiry row
claims.claim: AI-summary document expiry is under the selected meeting policy's Copilot and other AI section at the stated Intelligent Recap .docx expiration setting.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Meeting policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... Under Copilot and other AI, next to Set a default expiration time for Intelligent Recap .docx files for non-transcribed meetings

claims.where: controls[3].api; Governance controls: AI summary expiry row
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policyname> -IntelligentRecapDocxFileExpirationDays 180 sets AI-summary document expiry to 180 days.
claims.quote: The following example sets the default expiration time to 180 days. Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policyname> -IntelligentRecapDocxFileExpirationDays 180
claims.fix: Append to controls[3].note and its rendered note: 'The feature guide documents this setting as usable, but the Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference says IntelligentRecapDocxFileExpirationDays has not been fully released and will have no effect.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsmeetingpolicy alongside the existing feature guide.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Governance controls: AI summary expiry row
claims.claim: The AI-summary expiry setting accepts 1 to 9999 days, or -1 for no expiration.
claims.quote: You can specify a value from 1 to 9999 days, or -1 for no expiration.

claims.claim: Purview file retention takes precedence over Teams recording expiration.
claims.quote: A Teams meeting recording expiration policy can't delete a Teams meeting recording with a Purview retention policy until after the retention period is completed.

claims.claim: Remove-AIGeneratedKnowledge -ThreadId <String> -CallId <String> deletes a meeting memory file.
claims.quote: A Microsoft Teams admin can also delete a meeting memory file through PowerShell: ... Run the following command (ThreadId is required; CallId is optional) Remove-AIGeneratedKnowledge -ThreadId <String> -CallId <String>

claims.claim: A Teams administrator can delete a meeting memory file through PowerShell.
claims.quote: A Microsoft Teams admin can also delete a meeting memory file through PowerShell
